description: The pie chart visually represents the distribution of topics or domains associated with the automatic evaluation of attribution by large language models, as referenced in the paper. It is divided into eleven distinct segments, each labeled with a category and its corresponding percentage. The largest segment, colored blue, represents “AI/NLP Research” at 24.3%, followed by “Econ. & Fin.” in teal at 18.4%. Other notable segments include “History” and “Game&Anime,” both at 8.2%, “Daily Life” at 7.1%, “Science” at 6.7%, “Business” at 5.9%, “Pet & Animal” at 5.5%, and “Law” at 5.1%. Smaller segments include “Med & Health” at 5.5%, “Geography” at 2.7%, and “Math” at 1.2%. Each slice is connected to its label via a thin gray line, and percentages are displayed next to the category names. The chart uses a diverse color palette to distinguish categories, with no apparent ordering by size beyond visual grouping. No legend is present, as labels are directly linked to their respective slices.
